content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (first 5–10 days) and overestimates in late periods (last 5–10 days), suggesting a lag or delayed response to true trends.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct, leading to overprediction in the following 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: it tends to forecast prices back toward historical averages, missing sustained upward trends.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 10 days of the 30-day window, underestimating volatility and upward momentum.
- Model fails to capture the “late-cycle” surge in prices (last 5–10 days of 30d window), often underpredicting the final 5–7 days.
- When true prices rise sharply, model reacts with a delayed and exaggerated peak, then overcorrects downward — suggesting poor dynamic adjustment.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price increases during high-impact events (e.g., policy changes, supply shocks) — especially in the 10–20 day window.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sudden drops and overestimating gradual declines.
